courses.course_name: Fiber Optics: Installation, Splicing and Connectors
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​​This course introduces the student to the operation and installation of fiber optic communications systems. Students will gain hands on experience with various fiber components used in outside plant networks and i​ndoor premises cabling. Students will gain practical skills in connectorizing and splicing a variety of fiber cables. The theory portion of the course includes fundamental concepts of light theory, optical glass, connectors and splicing, as well as cable construction, handling, and installation procedures. The course emphasizes safety practices related to fiber optic work and covers potential hazards. Upon completion, students will have the necessary skills to construct basic fiber optic links using industry-standard tools and techniques. This course is the first of two required for earning the industry recognized Fiber Optic Association (FOA) Certified Fiber Optic Technician (CFOT) certificate. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

​​​This cours​e introduces students to advanced fiber optic topics including optical network designs, fiber optic analysis using link budgets, Optical Loss Test Sets (OLTS) and Optical Time Domain Reflectometers (OTDR). Troubleshooting is emphasized for new installations as well as maintaining existing systems as students gain hands-on experience testing optical components installed in outside plant systems to current ANSI/TIA (American National Standards Institute / Telecommunications Industry Association​) standards. For their final exam, students will write the Fiber Optic Association (FOA) industry recognized exam for Certified Fiber Optic Technician (CFOT).​ Successful completion of the exam will result in certification; if students require further attempts, they may register with the FOA separately.​ Prerequisite(s): 70% in TELX 3010

admission.raw: About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . Application processing Ongoing throughout the year.
